artiest/memphis-minnie.text:
Memphis Minnie was born Lizzie Douglas in 1897, probably in Tunica County, Mississippi, although she herself claimed to come from New Orleans. She was the eldest of thirteen children. She was given a guitar at the age of eight; by ten she could play the banjo and by eleven the guitar, and she was already playing at parties. In 1910 she ran away from home to Beale Street in Memphis. For years she played on street corners, and from 1916 to 1920 she toured the South with the Ringling Brothers Circus.

In 1929 she began performing with her second husband, Kansas Joe McCoy. A talent scout from Columbia Records discovered them in front of a barber shop, where they were playing for dimes. In New York, Columbia gave them the names Kansas Joe and Memphis Minnie. She later settled in Chicago, where she recorded prolifically for the producer Lester Melrose. She married Ernest Lawlars, known as Little Son Joe, who added a more rhythmic accompaniment to her guitar playing. In all, she recorded around two hundred songs, among them When the Levee Breaks, Me and My Chauffeur Blues, Bumble Bee and Nothing in Rambling.

Minnie was a guitarist, singer and songwriter who won herself an authoritative place on the stage as a woman. In 1933 she won a contest against Big Bill Broonzy in a Chicago nightclub. After the 1940s the tastes of the public changed, and she ended up with smaller labels. In 1957 she returned to Memphis with Lawlars, where she occasionally encouraged young blues musicians on the radio. She died in 1973.
artiest/memphis-minnie.listen: Listen to Me and My Chauffeur Blues and notice how the voice and the guitar answer each other: how confident does it sound, and how would you describe the guitar playing?

artiest/mental-theo.text:
Mental Theo is the stage name of Theo Nabuurs, a Dutch DJ and producer, born in 1965 in 's-Hertogenbosch. In the late 1980s he played in clubs in Mallorca and worked as an A&R manager at the record label Arcade. He then became known as a television presenter at TMF, RTL, SBS6 and Veronica. When Ruud de Wild left TMF as a VJ in 1998, he took over his programmes. Later he also started his own television production company, which made work for MTV and TMF. On the radio, from 2005 he presented programmes such as The Creepshow on the dance station Slam!FM.

As a musician he made harder dance music and performed as a duo with Charly Lownoise. His first solo album, Back Once Again, was released in 2005 and reached number 61 in the Dutch album chart. The second album, Jumpstyle Madness, came out in 2007 and belongs to jumpstyle, a dance style performed to fast hardstyle. In 2006, under the name Bazzheadz, he recorded a new version of Boten Anna by the Swedish producer Basshunter, under the title Now You're Gone. That single reached number 18 in the Danish chart. According to the Dutch Wikipedia, it is his biggest hit.

In 2021 he began working with Reinier Zonneveld, with the record Trek Drop as their first success. Mental Theo shows how a Dutch DJ in the 1990s and afterwards could move between club, television and radio, and in doing so gave harder dance music a face for a large audience.
artiest/mental-theo.listen: Listen to Now You're Gone and notice the relentless bass and the tight rhythm: how much of the melody of the original song is left?

artiest/mercedes-sosa.text: Mercedes Sosa, from San Miguel de Tucumán, was one of the voices of the nuevo cancionero, the renewed Argentine folk music. At the Cosquín festival in 1965, Jorge Cafrune brought her up on stage. In 1971 she sang Gracias a la vida at a tribute to Violeta Parra, and in 1977 she recorded an album of songs by Atahualpa Yupanqui. In 1979 she was arrested during a concert and went into exile.
artiest/mercedes-sosa.listen: Listen to her Gracias a la vida and compare it with the version by Violeta Parra: Sosa sings with a fuller voice and more slowly, like a hymn.

artiest/merry-clayton.text:
Merry Clayton is an American soul and gospel singer, born in 1948 in New Orleans. She got her first name because she was born on Christmas Day. She grew up in the New Zion Baptist Church, where her father was a minister. After moving to Los Angeles she met members of the Blossoms, who persuaded her to choose music. Her recording career began in 1962, at the age of fourteen, with a duet with Bobby Darin on his album You're the Reason I'm Living. In 1963 she recorded the first released version of The Shoop Shoop Song (It's in His Kiss).

She became famous for her duet with Mick Jagger on Gimme Shelter by the Rolling Stones, in 1969. According to Jagger, they asked her more or less by chance in the middle of the night in Los Angeles, because the band wanted a woman for the chorus. In 1970 she recorded a version of her own, which became the title of her first solo album. In 1972 she played the Acid Queen in the first London production of Tommy by The Who. She sang on Oh My My by Ringo Starr, on Sweet Home Alabama by Lynyrd Skynyrd and on Rock Creek Park by The Blackbyrds. She can also be heard with, among others, Carole King, Joe Cocker, Linda Ronstadt, Tom Jones and Neil Young. Later came albums such as Emotion in 2004 and Beautiful Scars in 2021.

Her strength lies in her gospel voice, which can lift a song from the background. The documentary 20 Feet from Stardom, which won an Oscar, shows how important backing singers are to popular music, and Clayton is at its centre.
artiest/merry-clayton.listen: Listen to Gimme Shelter by the Rolling Stones and notice the moment her voice comes to the fore: how does it cut through the rest of the band?

artiest/meshell-ndegeocello.text:
Meshell Ndegeocello is an American singer, songwriter, poet and bassist, born Michelle Lynn Johnson in West Berlin in 1968. Her father was an army officer and saxophonist. She grew up in Washington, where she attended the Duke Ellington School of the Arts. She took her surname herself; according to her, it means 'free like a bird' in Swahili. In the late 1980s she honed her craft on the go-go circuit of Washington, in bands such as Prophecy, Little Benny and the Masters and Rare Essence.

She was one of the first artists to sign with Maverick Records, where her debut Plantation Lullabies was released in 1993. It was followed by, among others, Peace Beyond Passion in 1996, Bitter in 1999, Comfort Woman in 2003, Weather in 2011 and Ventriloquism in 2018. Her biggest hit was Wild Night, a duet with John Mellencamp and a cover of the Van Morrison song. In 1996 she had a number one on the dance chart with Who Is He (And What Is He to You)?, a song by Bill Withers. She played bass on tracks by Madonna, the Rolling Stones and Alanis Morissette, and in 2016 she made the theme song for the series Queen Sugar. In 2023 she signed with Blue Note for The Omnichord Real Book.

Her music blends funk, soul, jazz, hip-hop, reggae and rock. In 2021 she presented a series on the Beatles and Black music on Sirius XM, and with her work on James Baldwin she showed how broad her interests ran. This makes her an example of a bassist who defines her own genre.
artiest/meshell-ndegeocello.listen: Listen to a track from Plantation Lullabies and notice the bass: how does it lead the song, and what in her voice would you say belongs to soul, and what to hip-hop?

artiest/metallica.text:
Metallica was formed in Los Angeles in 1981 by singer and guitarist James Hetfield and drummer Lars Ulrich. The band soon moved to San Francisco. Metallica is regarded as one of the 'Big Four' of thrash metal, together with Slayer, Megadeth and Anthrax. As a teenager, Ulrich was a fan of the British New Wave of British Heavy Metal. At their first concert in 1982 the band played four songs by Diamond Head, and Am I Evil? by that group remained in their repertoire for years.

After Kill 'Em All (1983) and Ride the Lightning (1984) came Master of Puppets (1986), recorded in Copenhagen with the producer Flemming Rasmussen. The title track lasts well over eight and a half minutes, has changes of time signature and a quiet, cleanly played middle section with a melodic solo. In September 1986 the bassist Cliff Burton was killed when the tour bus crashed in Sweden. Metallica reached the general public with the album Metallica (1991), the 'Black Album', produced by Bob Rock. In America that album went sixteen times platinum. Enter Sandman, with a riff by the guitarist Kirk Hammett, became the first single.

Metallica brought metal from small clubs to stadiums and the charts. Master of Puppets was the first metal record to be added by the American Library of Congress to the National Recording Registry. In 2000 the band sued the music service Napster for copyright infringement, a case that ended in a settlement. In 2022 the song Master of Puppets became popular again when it featured in the series Stranger Things. In 2009 the band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/metallica.listen: In Master of Puppets (1986) the guitars race along at a rapid tempo using only downstrokes (downpicking), until halfway through the band switches to a calm, cleanly played passage. Notice how the beat seems to slip slightly out of step each time before the riff returns.

artiest/metropole-orkest.text:
The Metropole Orkest is a jazz and pop orchestra from the Netherlands and the largest full-time ensemble of its kind in the world. It was founded in 1945 by Dolf van der Linden, at the urging of officials of the Dutch public broadcaster, which manages and subsidises the orchestra. Van der Linden led it for 35 years, until 1980. He was followed by, among others, Rogier van Otterloo, Dick Bakker, Vince Mendoza from 2005 to 2013, and Jules Buckley, from 2013.

The orchestra is a hybrid: it combines jazz, big band and classical symphony orchestra and consists of between fifty-two and ninety-seven musicians. It has a double rhythm section and can therefore handle many styles. It plays regularly at the North Sea Jazz festival and the Holland Festival, and on radio and television. Dutch film and television lean heavily on the orchestra for film music. It has played with Ella Fitzgerald, Dizzy Gillespie, Al Jarreau, Elvis Costello, Tori Amos, Bono, Brian Eno, Snarky Puppy, Jacob Collier and Within Temptation. In 2017 the public chose the band Epica from 650 suggestions for a joint project. Its albums include First in the Air from 1984, Made in Holland from 1987, Symphonic Jazz from 1997 and Parallel Universe from 2004.

In 2012 government funding was secured at the last moment, and in 2018 the orchestra warned that budget cuts had halved its work. The Metropole Orkest showed that a pop song with a string section, brass and a rhythm section can sound different from one with only a band.
artiest/metropole-orkest.listen: Listen to Symphonic Jazz or Kodachrome and try to hear which group carries the sound: the strings, the brass or the rhythm section.

artiest/mfsb.text:
MFSB officially stood for Mother Father Sister Brother. It was a group of more than thirty session musicians from Sigma Sound Studios in Philadelphia, who worked for the production team of Kenneth Gamble and Leon Huff and for the producer and arranger Thom Bell. They accompanied, among others, Harold Melvin and the Blue Notes, the O'Jays, the Stylistics, the Spinners, Wilson Pickett and Billy Paul. They were the house orchestra of the label Philadelphia International Records and created the Philly sound that dominated the charts in the early 1970s. Their first success was a number one in March 1973 as the backing band of the O'Jays on Love Train.

From 1972 they also recorded under their own name. Their debut album MFSB, from 1973, put them on the map, followed by Love Is the Message, Universal Love and Philadelphia Freedom. The second single, TSOP (The Sound of Philadelphia), was the theme tune of the television programme Soul Train. It was released in March 1974, topped the American pop and R&B charts and was certified gold in April.

The orchestra combined rhythm section, guitars, vibraphone, strings and horns. Later in the 1970s it was known for the hi-hat that coloured disco records by, among others, the Trammps and First Choice. TSOP helped to establish the disco sound. MFSB was formed in 1971 and disbanded in 1985.
artiest/mfsb.listen: Listen to TSOP (The Sound of Philadelphia) and notice the strings and the vibraphone above the supple rhythm section. Can you hear how the hi-hat drives the tempo along almost unnoticed?

artiest/mgmt.text:
MGMT is an American rock band that formed in 2002 in Middletown, Connecticut. Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser started the group during their first year at Wesleyan University. They did not set out to start a band, but simply listened together to music they liked. At first the group was called The Management, and in 2005 this became MGMT. Both are composers and multi-instrumentalists. VanWyngarden is the singer and lyricist. They experimented with noise rock and electronics before finding their own style.

In the autumn of 2006 the band signed with Columbia Records. With the producer Dave Fridmann, known for the Flaming Lips and Sleater-Kinney, they recorded their debut Oracular Spectacular in 2007. That album yielded three successful singles, including Time to Pretend. In 2008 they supported Radiohead in Manchester and played a headline tour of their own in Great Britain. In 2010 came Congratulations, recorded in Malibu with Pete Kember, also known as Sonic Boom of Spacemen 3, as producer and guide. The third album, MGMT, was released in 2013, again with Fridmann. Little Dark Age followed in 2018. The two core members wrote that album partly at a distance, by email. Loss of Life was released in 2024.

MGMT combines psychedelic rock with synthesizers and a style of writing that oscillates between irony and melody. The band shows how a duo of students, after a debut with big hits, chose stranger records, even though the record company and the public were not waiting for them at first.
artiest/mgmt.listen: Listen to Time to Pretend from Oracular Spectacular and notice the synthesizer and the vocals: does the song sound ironic or sweeping, or both?

artiest/mi-osc.text:
Miłość, which means 'Love' in Polish, was a Polish band from the yass scene, a distinctively Polish strand of free jazz. The group was founded in 1988 by Ryszard Tymon Tymański, a double bassist and guitarist and the former leader of the new wave band Sni Sredstvom Za Uklanianie. The music was free jazz with avant-garde influences. Out of it came, among others, the jazz bands of the Tricity, the area around Gdańsk, and Bydgoszcz, and a style that came to be called yass.

The line-up consisted of Tymański on double bass and vocals, Mikołaj Trzaska and Maciej Sikała on saxophone and Jacek Olter on drums. Jerzy Mazolewski played clarinet until 1991, after which the pianist Leszek Możdżer joined that same year. Their albums included Miłość in 1992, Taniec smoka in 1994 and Asthmatic in 1996. With the jazz musician Lester Bowie they recorded two albums: Not Two in 1995 and Talkin' About Life and Death in 1999. The band ceased to exist after Olter's death in 2002.

Miłość showed that free jazz in Poland could develop a distinctive, rough and playful sound, with punk and the avant-garde in its approach. Those who see the group as a beginning will find in it the roots of an entire generation of Polish jazz musicians, among them Możdżer, who later built an international career of his own.
artiest/mi-osc.listen: Listen to Not Two with Lester Bowie and notice how the saxophones, the trumpet and the double bass weave in and out of each other: who is following whom, and where do you hear unbridled freedom?

artiest/mia-farrow.text:
Mia Farrow is an American actress, born in 1945 in Los Angeles, the daughter of the director John Farrow and the actress Maureen O'Sullivan. She became known as Allison MacKenzie in the television series Peyton Place (1965). In 1966 she married Frank Sinatra; they divorced two years later. Her breakthrough as a film actress came with the lead role in Rosemary's Baby (1968) by Roman Polanski.

She appears in pop history through a journey in 1968. That year she studied Transcendental Meditation at the ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi in Rishikesh, India, where the Beatles were also staying. Donovan and Mike Love of The Beach Boys were there as well. The behaviour of her sister Prudence at the ashram gave John Lennon the idea for Dear Prudence. Lennon's Sexy Sadie is said to have been inspired by alleged advances made by the Maharishi towards Farrow, although others in the Beatles' circle later said that the story was invented. Farrow herself wrote in her memoirs that the Maharishi made her feel uncomfortable.

From 1980 to 1992 Farrow had a relationship with the director Woody Allen and appeared in more than ten of his films, such as Hannah and Her Sisters. Since 2000 she has been an ambassador for UNICEF and campaigns for children's rights in Africa and for the fight against polio, a disease she herself had as a child.
artiest/mia-farrow.listen: Listen to the guitar in Dear Prudence by the Beatles: Lennon plays a fingerpicking pattern that keeps circling round, like a mantra. Notice how the song slowly swells until the drums join in fully at the end.

artiest/mica-levi.text: Mica Levi was born in Surrey in 1987 and studied at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama in London. Levi first became known with the experimental pop band Micachu and the Shapes. The director Jonathan Glazer asked Levi to score Under the Skin (2013). The score consists of sliding, humming strings, with a short, recurring motif for the alien protagonist. Levi sought music that sounded strange and physical. For Jackie (2016) by Pablo Larraín, Levi wrote string music with slow glissandi that convey grief and distress; this earned an Oscar nomination. Again with Glazer came The Zone of Interest (2023), with strikingly little music: a dark overture and a closing piece.
artiest/mica-levi.listen: Notice the strings sliding between the notes: the unsteady pitch makes the music unsettling and physical.

artiest/micha-urbaniak.text: Michał Urbaniak was born in Warsaw in 1943 and played violin and saxophone. In the 1960s he played in Polish jazz groups and started a band of his own with the singer Urszula Dudziak, whom he married. In 1973 they moved to New York. There Urbaniak made records for Columbia such as Fusion (1974), in which jazz rock and Polish folk melodies come together. He played electric violin, often with effects. In 1986 he played violin on Tutu by Miles Davis. With his project Urbanator he brought jazz and hip-hop together in the early 1990s. He died in December 2025.
artiest/micha-urbaniak.listen: Listen to the electric violin, which sounds like a guitar in a rock band.

artiest/michael-brook.text:
Michael Brook is a Canadian guitarist, inventor, producer and film composer, born in 1952 in Toronto. He studied music and electronics at York University and worked as a technician at the Grant Avenue studio, which then belonged to the Lanois brothers. There he worked with Brian Eno, The Edge, Jon Hassell and Harold Budd. His first solo album, Hybrid, was released in 1985, with instrumental tracks featuring Indian and African elements. He lives in Los Angeles.

He became known as the inventor of the Infinite Guitar, a guitar whose notes sustain almost endlessly. The Edge used this instrument on The Joshua Tree by U2 in 1987. Brook worked with Pieter Nooten of Clan of Xymox on Sleeps With the Fishes in 1987, contributed to Set by Youssou N'Dour and Miss America by Mary Margaret O'Hara, and made the album Mustt Mustt with Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. For Night Song he received a Grammy nomination in 1996. He toured with Sylvian and Fripp, ending with a concert at the Royal Albert Hall in 1993, captured on Damage: Live.

As a film composer he wrote the music for, among others, Albino Alligator, Affliction, An Inconvenient Truth, Into the Wild, The Fighter, The Vow, Aloft and Brooklyn. For Into the Wild he received a Golden Globe nomination. His music combines electronics, world music and minimalism, and shows how a guitar without the usual attack can sound like an organ or a choir.
artiest/michael-brook.listen: Listen to a track from Hybrid and notice the guitar: can you hear how the notes ring on and blend into one another, as if it were not an ordinary guitar string?

artiest/michael-coleman.text:
Michael Coleman was born in 1891 near Ballymote in County Sligo, Ireland, the seventh child of a respected flute player. As a child he learned step dancing and the fiddle. In 1914 he left for the United States, where he lived with his aunt in Lowell, Massachusetts, performed briefly on the Keith vaudeville circuit and settled in New York in 1917. He married and had a daughter, Mary.

Between 1921 and 1936 Coleman recorded eighty commercial 78 rpm records for labels such as Columbia, Victor, Brunswick and Decca. He usually played with piano accompaniment, occasionally with tenor guitar or flute. In 1944 he recorded his last tracks, which were never commercially released. He died in 1945.

Coleman was regarded as the most famous exponent of the Sligo style of Irish fiddle music, which is fast, exuberant and richly ornamented, with fingered rolls and bowed triplets. He danced and played the fiddle at the same time. His records, made in New York, reached Irish emigrants in America and also travelled back to Ireland, where they became a model for young fiddle players. In this way he determined, for a large group of listeners, how Irish folk music was supposed to sound. Other Sligo fiddlers in New York in the same period were James Morrison, Paddy Killoran and Paddy Sweeney.
artiest/michael-coleman.listen: Listen to Tarbolton / The Longford Collector / The Sailor's Bonnet and notice the fast tempo and the ornaments in the melody. Can you hear the moment where one tune passes into the next?

artiest/michael-giacchino.text: Michael Giacchino (born in New Jersey in 1967) studied film and first worked at game studios. For the game Medal of Honor (1999) he wrote a full orchestral score, still unusual for games at the time. Through J.J. Abrams he moved into television, with Alias and Lost (2004). For Pixar he made The Incredibles (2004), in the style of the big-band spy music of the 1960s. For Up (2009) he won an Oscar. The theme Married Life is a waltz that tells the story of an entire marriage in a few minutes. For The Batman (2022) he built everything from a four-note motif. Giacchino thinks in strong themes.
artiest/michael-giacchino.listen: Listen in Married Life to how a single waltz melody changes from playful to sad, through instrumentation, tempo and harmony alone.

artiest/michael-jackson.text:
Michael Jackson was born on 29 August 1958 in Gary, Indiana, the eighth of ten children. His father, a crane operator who played guitar himself, formed a band with his sons. So Michael was already on stage at the age of six, as lead singer of what would become The Jackson 5. With that group he scored his first hits at Motown, and as a teenager he also began a solo career.

His great breakthrough as an adult artist came with Off the Wall (1979). Thriller (1982) followed, the best-selling album in history. The videos for Thriller, Beat It and Billie Jean changed what a video could be: short films with dance in the leading role. Bad (1987) was the first album to produce five number ones on the American Billboard Hot 100. Dangerous (1991), HIStory (1995) and Invincible (2001) followed.

Jackson blended soul, funk, disco, pop and rock and delivered it with a recognisable, high voice and sharp rhythms. On stage he made dance moves such as the moonwalk world famous. His success broke through racial barriers in the American music industry and made him a dominant figure worldwide. From the mid-1980s onwards his private life became increasingly a subject of debate, partly because of allegations of child abuse. In 2005 he was acquitted of these charges in a trial. During preparations for a series of comeback concerts he died on 25 June 2009 of an overdose of an anaesthetic given to him by his doctor.
artiest/michael-jackson.listen: Listen to Beat It (1983). Notice how a tight, danceable pop rhythm combines with a heavy rock guitar, and how the guitar solo halfway through the song briefly demands all the attention.

artiest/michael-kamen.text: Michael Kamen was born in New York in 1948. He studied at the High School of Music & Art and at the Juilliard School. In 1968 he founded the New York Rock & Roll Ensemble with, among others, Mark Snow. Throughout his career he continued to work between rock and orchestra. He contributed to The Wall by Pink Floyd and arranged for Eric Clapton, Bryan Adams, Queen and Metallica. With Metallica he won a Grammy for S&M (1999). His film work includes Brazil (1985), the Lethal Weapon series (from 1987), the Die Hard series (from 1988), Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves (1991) and Mr. Holland's Opus (1995). For the television series Band of Brothers (2001) he wrote the theme. He died in London in 2003.
artiest/michael-kamen.listen: In Band of Brothers, notice the calm, solemn theme in strings and brass, which expresses mourning rather than heroism.

artiest/michael-mantler.text:
Michael Mantler was born in Vienna in 1943 and is an Austrian trumpeter and composer of avant-garde jazz and contemporary music. In the early 1960s he studied trumpet and musicology at the Vienna academy of music and the university, and then at Berklee College in Boston. In 1964 he moved to New York and joined the Jazz Composers Guild, together with Roswell Rudd, Archie Shepp and Cecil Taylor. In 1972 he founded the New Music Distribution Service, which served many independent labels for almost twenty years. With Carla Bley, to whom he was married from 1965 to 1991, he started WATT Records. Their daughter Karen Mantler also became a musician.

Mantler recorded many solo albums, feeling himself more a composer than a bandleader. He set texts by writers such as Samuel Beckett to music, including on No Answer in 1974 and Many Have No Speech in 1987, with vocals by rock musicians such as Jack Bruce. On Something There in 1983 he worked with the strings of the London Symphony Orchestra. The album Movies from 1978 sounded, according to the critic Robert Christgau, like the ultimate soundtrack demo. From 1977 to 1985 he played in the Carla Bley Band.

In 1991 he moved to Europe and divided his time between Copenhagen and the south of France. He received commissions from European radio orchestras and wrote, among other works, the near-opera School of Understanding and One Symphony. His work shows how jazz, chamber music and literature can flow into one another, with rock singers in a classical setting.
artiest/michael-mantler.listen: Listen to a track from Many Have No Speech and notice the singer delivering Beckett's text: how does the voice relate to the restrained accompaniment?

artiest/michael-mcdonald.text:
Michael McDonald was born in 1952 in Ferguson, Missouri, near St. Louis. As a schoolboy he played in local bands and in 1970 he was discovered while playing with a group called Blue. In 1974 he joined the touring band of Steely Dan, as a Wurlitzer electric piano player and singer. He sang lead on Show Biz Kids and the last verse of Pretzel Logic. By his own account he got the job because he could sing all the high parts, which appealed to Donald Fagen.

In April 1975 the Doobie Brothers brought him in as a temporary replacement for the singer Tom Johnston, who had fallen ill. It went so well that he stayed. He sang lead on songs such as Takin' It to the Streets, Little Darling (I Need You), It Keeps You Runnin' and Minute by Minute. What a Fool Believes became a number one in the United States and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year in 1980, shared with Kenny Loggins. Meanwhile he sang and played as a session musician for Christopher Cross, Bonnie Raitt, Toto and Kenny Loggins.

His solo album If That's What It Takes was released in 1982 and contained the hit I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near). Later came, among others, Blue Obsession, Motown in 2003 and Soul Speak in 2008. His voice, soulful and with a dark warmth, became a trademark of the smooth West Coast sound. He also collaborated with, among others, Aretha Franklin, Van Halen and Grizzly Bear.
artiest/michael-mcdonald.listen: Listen to What a Fool Believes by the Doobie Brothers and notice the piano rhythm and the choral singing around it: how does McDonald's voice sound among them?

artiest/michael-moore.text:
Michael Moore was born in 1954 in Eureka, California, and is an American jazz saxophonist and clarinettist who has lived in the Netherlands since 1982. His father was a semi-professional musician. Moore studied at Humboldt State and graduated in 1977 from the New England Conservatory, where he was taught by Jaki Byard and Gunther Schuller and was a classmate of Marty Ehrlich. He played in all kinds of settings, mainly for theatre and dance.

In the Netherlands he became a fixture on the jazz circuit. He plays in the Clusone Trio, together with the cellist Ernst Reijseger and the drummer Han Bennink. That trio was intended for a single performance at a festival in Clusone in Italy, but went on to tour for years and recorded six albums, including one of freely played compositions by Irving Berlin. His first record as a leader came out in 1992, and with Chicoutimi in 1994 his reputation as a composer grew. That album featured a trio without drums with Fred Hersch and Mark Helias and recalls the trios of Jimmy Giuffre. In 1986 he won the VPRO/Boy Edgar Prize, the most important jazz prize in the Netherlands, and in 1991 he founded the label Ramboy Records.

Moore also plays in Jewels and Binoculars, a trio that arranges songs by Bob Dylan, and since 2005 has led a quintet with Eric Vloeimans, Marc van Roon, Paul Berner and Owen Hart Jr. In 2013 he performed with InstanPool, a group that makes improvised music with electronics. In this way he showed how an American jazz musician could feel at home in the Dutch circuit.
artiest/michael-moore.listen: Listen to a track by the Clusone Trio and notice how saxophone or clarinet, cello and drums play off one another: who is accompanying whom, and where do you hear humour?

artiest/michael-nyman.text: Michael Nyman was born in London in 1944 and studied at the Royal Academy of Music. He first worked as a music critic and was one of the first to apply the term minimalism to music. With his own Michael Nyman Band, with saxophones and amplified strings, he developed a hard, energetic form of minimal music. For the director Peter Greenaway he built scores on early music: in The Draughtsman's Contract (1982) on bass lines by Henry Purcell, in Drowning by Numbers (1988) on a slow movement by Mozart. His greatest success was The Piano (1993) by Jane Campion. There his piano music, partly based on Scottish folk songs, gives the silent protagonist a voice.
artiest/michael-nyman.listen: Notice the firm, repeated bass line beneath the melody: this is how Nyman builds new music on old Baroque and Classical patterns.

artiest/michael-nyman-band.text:
The Michael Nyman Band, formerly known as the Campiello Band, came into being in 1976 as a street band for a production of Il Campiello by Carlo Goldoni, directed by Bill Bryden at the Old Vic in London. When the production ended, the musicians did not want to part. So their leader, Michael Nyman, began writing music for them, starting with In Re Don Giovanni. The line-up varied, and whoever played on an album was often listed as a permanent member.

The first album on a professional label was Michael Nyman from 1981, mainly with music for the early films of Peter Greenaway. Greenaway's The Draughtsman's Contract, Drowning by Numbers and The Cook The Thief His Wife & Her Lover formed the core of their work in the 1980s, alongside The Kiss and Other Movements. The album The Essential Michael Nyman Band from 1992 looks like a compilation, but contains concert versions of film pieces that had been revised over many years. In 1993 the band played together with an orchestra for the first time, in MGV: Musique à Grand Vitesse, written for the opening of a TGV line. Later soundtracks such as Practical Magic, Ravenous, The End of the Affair and The Libertine were released under the name of the group or of the Michael Nyman Orchestra. Songbook was also released in 1991 and The Suit and the Photograph in 1998.

The group played Nyman's music in a distinctive, amplified sound, with strings, saxophones and a driving rhythm, bringing minimal music out of the concert hall. Members such as John Harle and Alexander Balanescu later made albums of their own.
artiest/michael-nyman-band.listen: Listen to a piece from The Draughtsman's Contract or The Cook The Thief His Wife & Her Lover and notice the repetition: how does the rhythm of the strings build tension?

artiest/michael-price.text:
Michael Price is an English composer and pianist. He is the son of physics and biology teachers and studied music on the Tonmeister course at Surrey University, where in 1990 he won the PRS composition prize. Before becoming a composer he worked in film and television music as a producer, arranger and music editor, much of it alongside the film composer Michael Kamen. His first film work was in 1996, when Kamen asked him to programme and orchestrate the electronic sounds for Event Horizon. This grew into a five-year collaboration, with concerts in Berlin, New York, San Francisco and Geneva.

As a music editor he worked on The Lord of the Rings by Peter Jackson, Love Actually and Nanny McPhee, and in 2001 he won a Golden Reel Award for The Fellowship of the Ring. As a composer he wrote the music for thirty-one films and for television series such as Unforgotten. Together with David Arnold he composed the music for all thirteen episodes of the BBC series Sherlock, from 2010, and in 2015 for Jekyll and Hyde. He also wrote music for the documentaries The Possibility of Hope and The Shock Doctrine by Alfonso Cuarón.

His first work outside film was in 2012, a collection of string quartets, A Stillness, on Erased Tapes. The albums Entanglement in 2015, Diary in 2017, thirty improvisations for solo piano, and Tender Symmetry in 2018, recorded at seven National Trust locations, followed. In 2021 The Hope of Better Weather was released, with reworkings by, among others, Yann Tiersen. In this way he moved between the television studio and modern classical music.
artiest/michael-price.listen: Listen to a piece from Diary and notice the loose, free-flowing piano music: how can you hear that it is improvised, and which mood persists?

artiest/michael-rother.text:
Michael Rother is a German guitarist and keyboard player, born in 1950 in Hamburg. He went to school in, among other places, England, Karachi and Düsseldorf; the Pakistani music he heard in Karachi later worked its way into his own work. In 1971 he played briefly with the drummer Klaus Dinger in a line-up of Kraftwerk, when Ralf Hütter was temporarily away. That same year the two started their own group in Düsseldorf, Neu!.

Neu! made the albums Neu! (1972), Neu! 2 (1973) and Neu! '75 (1975), each time with the producer Conny Plank, who is often called the hidden band member. The group is known for the motorik: a simple, driving 4/4 beat with a lot of bass drum, which always seems to be moving forwards. Dinger developed that rhythm together with Jaki Liebezeit of Can. Above it Rother laid his guitar and keyboard parts. Musicians such as David Bowie, Brian Eno, Sonic Youth, Stereolab, Thom Yorke and the drummer Stephen Morris of Joy Division later cited Neu! as an influence.

With Hans-Joachim Roedelius and Dieter Moebius of Cluster, Rother then formed the group Harmonia, which released two albums in 1974 and 1975. Recordings with Brian Eno from 1976 went missing and were not released until 1997. From 1977 Rother made solo albums, beginning with Flammende Herzen, followed by Sterntaler (1978) and Katzenmusik (1979); Jaki Liebezeit played drums on all three. In 2022 he celebrated fifty years of Neu! with concerts in Berlin and London.
artiest/michael-rother.listen: In Hallogallo, the opening track of the first Neu! album (1972), listen to Klaus Dinger's beat: the same straight, driving rhythm for minutes on end. Notice how Rother lets layers of guitar come and go above it, so that the track changes while the rhythm stays the same.

artiest/michael-salvatori.text:
Michael Salvatori was born in 1954 in Elmhurst, Illinois, and is an American composer. He is best known as the partner of Martin O'Donnell in composing the music for the Halo game series. After his studies he borrowed money from the bank to build a studio in his basement in Wheaton. There he recorded his first solo album, Waiting for Autumn. During his student years he wrote music for his own rock band and became friends with O'Donnell. When O'Donnell was offered the chance in Chicago to score a colleague's film, he offered to share the work with Salvatori, who had a studio of his own. In this way they became partners and founded the company TotalAudio.

For the studio Bungie they made the music for Myth: The Fallen Lords and Myth II: Soulblighter together, and then for Halo. When O'Donnell joined Bungie as an employee in 1999, Salvatori stayed behind to manage the business side of TotalAudio. He came on board in 2009 for Halo 3: ODST, for which the team decided to make only new music, without the old Halo themes. He co-wrote the music for Halo 2, Halo 3 and Halo Reach. With O'Donnell he composed Destiny from 2014, which that year won an award from the National Academy of Video Game Trade Reviewers, and the expansions The Taken King and Rise of Iron. He also wrote music for Destiny 2 in 2017 and the expansions Forsaken, Shadowkeep, Beyond Light, The Witch Queen, Lightfall and The Final Shape.

In October 2023 he was laid off by Bungie in a round of cost-cutting. His work belongs to the game music that was also released on album, independently of the game.
artiest/michael-salvatori.listen: Listen to a track from Halo 3: ODST: Original Soundtrack and notice how it differs from the grand Halo themes: which instruments give it its own, new atmosphere?

artiest/michael-stein.text:
Michael Stein is an American composer and electronic musician who works with Kyle Dixon. They began together in the electronic music scene of Austin, Texas. In 2009 they formed the synthesizer band Survive with Adam Jones and Mark Donica. That music is associated with analogue synthesizers, playing live on hardware and electronic compositions influenced by the music of horror and science-fiction films. Stein sees Survive as one part of a broader musical series, alongside the work for film and television that the duo makes under the name Short Hour.

Their big breakthrough came with Stranger Things. The creators, the Duffer Brothers, discovered the music of Survive and used one of its tracks in an early pitch trailer. The duo was then commissioned to write the music for the series. Only the two of them did it, because the production could not afford the whole band. The music was released on several soundtrack albums on Lakeshore Records and Invada Records. Their title music won a Primetime Emmy Award in 2017, and the first two volumes received Grammy nominations.

Apart from Stranger Things they composed the music for the virtual reality series Spheres from 2018, the short film A Different Beyond, the British series Butterfly and films such as The Hole in the Fence and Lost in the Night. They also wrote music for the installation Convergence Station by Meow Wolf in Denver. In 2026 they toured Europe with Stranger Things music, in a show with light and sculpted fog. Their work shows how analogue synthesizers from the 1970s and 1980s could once again carry a major television series.
artiest/michael-stein.listen: Listen to the main theme of Stranger Things and notice the synthesizer arpeggios: how does the rhythm of the repetition build tension, and which instrument do you hear first?

artiest/michael-stipe.text:
Michael Stipe is the singer and lyricist of the American rock band R.E.M. He was born in 1960 in Decatur, Georgia. Around 1980 he was studying in Athens, Georgia, where he met the guitarist Peter Buck in a record shop. With the drummer Bill Berry and the bassist Mike Mills they started R.E.M.; they took the name from a dictionary.

The first single, Radio Free Europe, was a success on American college radio, and the debut album Murmur (1983) received glowing reviews. In those early years Stipe sang in a mumble, with cryptic lyrics that were hard to follow. In the mid-1980s his singing became clearer and the lyrics more direct. On Document (1987) and Green (1988) they also became more political. With Out of Time (1991), with the single Losing My Religion, and Automatic for the People (1992), R.E.M. broke through definitively to the general public, without letting go of their roots in alternative rock.

Stipe also shaped the image of the band: he chose the sleeves and directed many of the videos. He is also a photographer and film producer. In 1997 Berry left, after which R.E.M. continued as a trio; in 2011 the band split up on amicable terms. Stipe afterwards released solo singles such as Your Capricious Soul (2019) and Drive to the Ocean (2020).
artiest/michael-stipe.listen: In It's the End of the World as We Know It (And I Feel Fine), listen to the verses, in which Stipe rattles off words and names at high speed, almost without drawing breath. Notice the contrast with the chorus, where the singing suddenly becomes calm and melodic.

artiest/michel-legrand.text: Michel Legrand studied at the Paris Conservatoire with Nadia Boulanger and then became a jazz arranger. In 1958 he made the album Legrand Jazz with, among others, Miles Davis and John Coltrane. In the nouvelle vague he wrote for Agnès Varda, Jean-Luc Godard and above all Jacques Demy. Les parapluies de Cherbourg (1964) by Demy is sung throughout, even the ordinary dialogue. Legrand built the film from jazz harmony and recurring melodies. In Les demoiselles de Rochefort (1967) he opted for swing and big dance numbers. In Hollywood he won an Oscar for The Windmills of Your Mind from The Thomas Crown Affair (1968).
artiest/michel-legrand.listen: Notice the jazz chords beneath the melodies and how ordinary dialogue in Cherbourg is set to music as song.

artiest/mick-fleetwood.text:
Mick Fleetwood is an English drummer, born in 1947 in Redruth, Cornwall. He spent part of his childhood in Egypt and Norway and left school at fifteen to become a drummer in London. He taught himself to play. In 1967 he played briefly with John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers. Shortly afterwards the guitarist Peter Green asked him and the bassist John McVie to join a new band: Fleetwood Mac, named after the surnames of the drummer and the bassist.

Fleetwood Mac began as a British blues band, but changed radically in the 1970s. With Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks on board, the group became a pop rock band. The album Rumours (1977) spent 31 weeks at the top of the American album chart, had already sold more than ten million copies by March 1978 and won the Grammy for Album of the Year. During that period there were great tensions within the band, and Fleetwood is seen as the one who held the group together. He and McVie are the only ones who play on every Fleetwood Mac studio album.

Fleetwood is not regarded as a virtuoso, but as a disciplined drummer who adapts to every style. It was precisely that calm that gave a band full of strong personalities something to hold on to. In 1981 he made the solo album The Visitor, with influences from African music. He also played drums on solo records by his bandmates and had small roles in films and series. In 1998 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Fleetwood Mac.
artiest/mick-fleetwood.listen: In Go Your Own Way, listen to the drums in the verses: Fleetwood does not play an ordinary rock beat, but a stuttering pattern on the toms, with the accents in unexpected places. Notice how the rhythm becomes straighter and fuller in the chorus.

artiest/mick-gordon.text: Mick Gordon comes from Mackay in Queensland, Australia. As a teenager he played jazz and blues on guitar. In the games world he began as a sound designer at Pandemic Studios. After Need for Speed: Shift (2009) and Killer Instinct (2013) he wrote the music for Wolfenstein: The New Order (2014). For Doom (2016), id Software at first asked him not to use guitars or metal. Gordon sent low sine tones through chains of effects units and mixed them with white noise. Later he was allowed to use guitar after all: a nine-string guitar, together with the sound of the chainsaw from the original Doom. The score won the award for Best Music at The Game Awards in 2016. After Doom Eternal (2020) he fell into a public dispute with id Software.
artiest/mick-gordon.listen: Listen to how heavy, distorted synthesizers and the low nine-string guitar together form a rhythmic wall of sound, in which sound design and melody merge.

artiest/mick-jagger.text:
Mick Jagger is the singer and one of the founders of The Rolling Stones. He was born in 1943 in Dartford, in the English county of Kent. As a child he sang in the church choir and listened to singers on the radio. In the mid-1950s he started a little band that played songs by Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry and Bo Diddley. In 1961 he ran into his old schoolmate Keith Richards again at Dartford station. Jagger had records by Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters with him, and that was how their partnership began. With Brian Jones they played with Alexis Korner's Blues Incorporated. In July 1962 they performed for the first time as the Rollin' Stones, named after a song by Muddy Waters. Jagger then gave up his studies at the London School of Economics.

At first the band mainly played American rhythm and blues. At the urging of their manager Andrew Loog Oldham, Jagger and Richards began writing their own songs. With The Last Time and (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction the Stones acquired the image of rebellious troublemakers, as opposed to the sweet Beatles. The songwriting duo of Jagger and Richards became one of the most successful in rock history.

Jagger's raw voice and his exuberant performances, together with Richards's guitar, became the band's trademark. He brought style and sex appeal to rock 'n' roll and became a model for later frontmen. He also made solo albums, such as She's the Boss (1985), and in 1985 sang Dancing in the Street with David Bowie. In 1989 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the Stones. In 2003 he was knighted.
artiest/mick-jagger.listen: Listen to Miss You by The Rolling Stones from 1978. Notice the bass line that jumps back and forth in octaves as in disco, Jagger's falsetto, and the harmonica that plays the melody.

artiest/mick-ronson.text:
Mick Ronson was born in 1946 in Kingston upon Hull and became an English guitarist, songwriter, arranger and producer. As a child he had classical lessons on piano, recorder, violin and later harmonium. At first he wanted to be a cellist, but chose the guitar when he discovered the music of Duane Eddy. In 1965 he moved to London to look for work. In early 1970 Bowie's drummer John Cambridge tracked him down in Hull, where he was marking out rugby pitches as a council gardener, and brought him to Bowie's group The Hype.

Ronson became the guitarist of the Spiders from Mars and played on five studio albums by David Bowie, including Hunky Dory and The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars. He also wrote string arrangements and gave much of the sound of those years its character. Aladdin Sane and Pin Ups followed. Together with Bowie he produced Transformer by Lou Reed, on which he played guitar and piano and wrote strings, with Walk on the Wild Side as its best-known track. Later he played on four albums with Ian Hunter and toured with Van Morrison and Bob Dylan. His own album Slaughter on 10th Avenue from 1974 reached number nine in the British album chart.

In 1994 Bowie called him the perfect counterpart to the character of Ziggy: a down-to-earth Northerner beside a glamorous rock star. Ronson died in 1993. Rolling Stone ranked him at number 64 in 2003 and at number 41 in 2012 among the greatest guitarists.
artiest/mick-ronson.listen: Listen to Ziggy Stardust by David Bowie and notice the guitar riff and the solo work: how does Ronson's guitar sound, rough yet melodic, beside Bowie's voice?

artiest/mick-talbot.text:
Mick Talbot was born in 1958 in Wimbledon, London, and is an English keyboard player, songwriter, composer and producer. He became known as a co-founder of The Style Council, the soul and jazz collective he formed with Paul Weller, the former singer of The Jam. They began working together in 1982, and the first records came out in early 1983. Earlier, Talbot had played with the Merton Parkas, a group from the mod revival of the late 1970s, and with The Bureau, in whose video for Only for Sheep he appears.

After the end of The Style Council in March 1990 he continued to play with Weller on his solo albums. With his former bandmate Steve White he made albums as Talbot/White. In 1995 and 1996 Talbot and White released the instrumental albums United States of Mind and Off the Beaten Track, with the bassist Yolanda Charles and guests, including Weller. He also played with White and the bassist Damon Minchella, formerly of Ocean Colour Scene, in the jazz-funk band The Players. He was also a member of Dexys Midnight Runners in 1980 and of Dexys from 2003 to 2013, played keyboards with Galliano and on the album Road to Freedom by Young Disciples from 1991, and toured with Candi Staton in 2009. In 2014 he worked with Wilko Johnson and Roger Daltrey on Going Back Home.

His Hammond organ and piano gave the Style Council a jazzy, soulful colour that went beyond the guitar pop of the time. In this way he showed how a 1980s mod could build a soul sound of his own. His album Back To Business was released in 2022.
artiest/mick-talbot.listen: Listen to a track by The Style Council and notice Talbot's keyboards: can you hear whether it is the organ or the piano, and how does it give a pop song its soul and jazz colour?

artiest/mickey-baker.text:
Mickey Baker was born in 1925 in Louisville, Kentucky, and grew into one of the most sought-after session guitarists in American rhythm and blues. At the age of eleven he was placed in an orphanage, from which he often ran away. At sixteen he stayed on in New York and worked as a labourer and dishwasher. He wanted to become a jazz musician and at first had the trumpet in mind, but for fourteen dollars he could find only guitars in a pawnshop. He took lessons from various teachers and by 1949 was already playing with a combo of his own.

In California he saw the blues guitarist Pee Wee Crayton perform, and that introduced him to bending strings: for him the blues was at that time mainly a way of earning money. Back in the East he recorded for Savoy, King and Atlantic Records and played sessions with Doc Pomus, The Drifters, Ray Charles, Ruth Brown, Big Joe Turner, Louis Jordan, Coleman Hawkins and Dion. Inspired by the success of Les Paul and Mary Ford, in the mid-1950s he formed the duo Mickey & Sylvia with his guitar pupil Sylvia Robinson. Their hit Love Is Strange was released in 1956. His solo album The Wildest Guitar came out in 1959.

Later he moved to France, where he worked with Ronnie Bird and Chantal Goya and remained for the rest of his life. He also wrote influential guitar tutor books, played at the Roskilde Festival in 1975 and recorded albums for Big Bear Records in the 1970s. He died in 2012. His playing can be heard running through many records of the 1950s, even though his name is not on the front.
artiest/mickey-baker.listen: Listen to Love Is Strange by Mickey & Sylvia and notice Baker's guitar line: what does the guitar do between the vocals of the two, and how does he keep the rhythm light?

artiest/mickey-en-sylvia.text:
Mickey & Sylvia was an American R&B duo of the guitarist Mickey Baker and Sylvia Vanterpool, who later became known as Sylvia Robinson. Baker gave music lessons and set up the duo in the mid-1950s, following the example of the successful duo Les Paul and Mary Ford. From 1954 they recorded together, in 1955 the first records appeared under the name Mickey & Sylvia, and at Groove Records they became the label's first big sellers.

In November 1956 Love Is Strange was released. Sylvia had heard the song from Bo Diddley, with whom she had performed in Washington, and with his blessing the duo recorded a version of their own. In early 1957 it was number 1 on the American R&B chart and number 11 on the pop chart. More than a million copies were sold. The song lives on in films such as Dirty Dancing and Casino.

In 1958 they split up, although they worked together occasionally afterwards and in 1961 started the label Willow Records. Baker left for France in the 1960s. For Sylvia the duo was the beginning of a long career in the music industry. In 1973 she had a hit with Pillow Talk, and later she was a co-founder of the rap label Sugar Hill Records. Through her, a line thus runs from the rhythm and blues of the 1950s to the beginnings of hip-hop.
artiest/mickey-en-sylvia.listen: In Love Is Strange, listen to Mickey Baker's guitar riff at the beginning, which returns throughout the song. Notice also the spoken section in the middle, in which Mickey and Sylvia talk to each other instead of singing.

artiest/mickey-hart.text:
Mickey Hart was born in 1943 as Michael Steven Hartman in Brooklyn and grew up in Inwood, New York. His mother Leah was a drummer, his father Lenny a champion of rudimental drumming, but he left the family when Mickey was a toddler. At school he mastered the rudiments, with help from his teacher Arthur Jones. Performances by Tito Puente and the music of the Nigerian drummer Babatunde Olatunji shaped him. In 1961 he joined the air force, where he drummed with The Airmen of Note, a big band of the air force band.

In September 1967 he joined the Grateful Dead, alongside the drummer Bill Kreutzmann, with whom he earned the nickname the rhythm devils. His interest in polyrhythm and exotic percussion became a fixed part of the arrangements in what was later called the primal Dead era of 1968 and 1969. He left the band in 1971 by agreement, and returned in 1974, until the group stopped in 1995. Afterwards he played with The Other Ones, The Dead and Dead & Company.

Besides the Dead he was a solo artist, percussionist and author of books on drumming traditions, and he continued to immerse himself in ethnomusicology and world music. He worked with the American Folklife Center of the Library of Congress and the Smithsonian on documenting musical traditions that were in danger of disappearing. In 1991 he produced Planet Drum, which spent 26 weeks at number one on the Billboard World Music chart and won the first Grammy for Best World Music Album. His solo records are percussive and lean towards new age. In 2009 he was inducted into the Hall of Fame of the Percussive Arts Society.
artiest/mickey-hart.listen: Listen to a track from Planet Drum and notice the layers of percussion: how many different drums and rhythms do you hear at once, and how do they fit together?

artiest/midge-ure.text:
Midge Ure, properly James Ure, is a Scottish singer, guitarist and producer, born in 1953 in Cambuslang near Glasgow. His stage name is Jim, pronounced backwards. In the 1970s he played in Slik, who were number 1 in England in 1976 with Forever and Ever, and then in Rich Kids, with Glen Matlock of the Sex Pistols. Around 1980 he was also in Visage, who had a hit with Fade to Grey.

In 1979 Ure became the new singer of Ultravox, after the departure of John Foxx. Under his leadership the band enjoyed its most successful years. Vienna, released in January 1981, spent four weeks at number two in England and became one of the best-selling singles of that year. Ultravox mixed rock with synthesizers and so belonged to the synth-pop and new wave of the early 1980s.

In November 1984 Ure wrote Do They Know It's Christmas? together with Bob Geldof for Band Aid, a group of British pop stars who raised money for the famine in Ethiopia. The single sold 3.7 million copies in England on its first release and is one of the best-selling singles there of all time. In July 1985 Ure also organised the benefit concert Live Aid with Geldof. That same year he was at number 1 as a solo artist with If I Was. In 2005 he was appointed OBE for his services to music and charity.
artiest/midge-ure.listen: In Do They Know It's Christmas?, listen to how a different star sings a line each time, so that the song sounds like a row of famous voices one after another. Notice the ending, in which all the voices keep repeating the same short phrase together.

artiest/mighty-sparrow.text:
Slinger Francisco, known as The Mighty Sparrow, was born in 1935 in the Grenadian fishing village of Grand Roy and grew up in Laventille, a district of Port of Spain in Trinidad. At fourteen he played in a steelband during carnival. He got the name Little Sparrow because he moved about during his performances, which the older singers found strange. Later this became Mighty Sparrow. His first performance as a carnival singer followed in 1954, his first recordings in 1955, including High Cost of Living and Race Track.

The breakthrough came in 1956 with Jean and Dinah, also known as Yankees Gone, a song about the departure of the American troops from Trinidad. With it he won both the Road March and the title of Calypso King. The prize money was forty dollars, compared with thousands of dollars for the carnival queen, and in protest he wrote Carnival Boycott. He won the Road March eight times, became Calypso King eight times and twice Calypso King of Kings. His records from the 1950s, such as Calypso Carnival (1958) and Sparrow in Hi-Fi (1959), brought calypso to a wider audience.

Calypso is the singing tradition of Trinidad, full of wordplay, mockery and commentary on current events. Sparrow added an energetic stage show to it, in which he compared himself to James Brown, and showed how a critical lyric can sound like dance music. He became known as the Calypso King of the World. According to the source, he died in 2026.
artiest/mighty-sparrow.listen: Listen to Jean and Dinah and notice what he sings about the American soldiers and the girls. Can you hear how mockery and dance rhythm come together in one song?
